cues: Why does marriage matter to men?
Nock borrows an old argument from the French sociologist Émile Durkheim.
In modern societies basic needs are mostly met, so desire moves on: to comfort, luxury, prestige.
And those wants have no natural limit; satisfied, they demand more.
So the central problem is setting legitimate limits on desire, and Durkheim says marriage does it.
It is an organ of society that ties a man to one partner, gives his need for love a strictly definite object, closes the horizon, and so gives him moral equilibrium.
